deep.reconstruction:
The page contains no derivations, formulas or computations. It is a sequence of four aphorisms on the philosophy and methodology of mathematics. It continues the reflections on the previous page (mathematics as the science of divisibility and of greater/less/between; the 'marriage' of number theory and function theory in class field theory and complex multiplication). It leads into the next page, on the 'two giants', the concept of magnitude and the concept of decomposition.

(1) Goethe, Faust I (Mephistopheles to the Student): 'Grau, teurer Freund, ist alle Theorie, und grün des Lebens goldner Baum.' Hilbert remarks that people quote this while forgetting that it is the Devil who says it, and that even he does not mean it seriously. It is a defence of theory.

(2) Whoever considers only magnitudes (function theory, geometry, mathematical physics), and whoever considers only the formal (divisibility, reducibility, number theory), 'hobbles on one leg each'. How differently the healthy person strides, who can use both legs. This is the same dichotomy as the next page's 'Grössenbegriff' versus 'Zerlegungsbegriff', whose chief weapons are the irrational number and the ideal respectively.

(3) 'The formula must be our servant, not we the servants of formulas.'

(4) On 'purity of method' (Reinheit der Methode). One speaks much of purity of method. Yet what is unsatisfying is not, as is often wrongly assumed, the foreignness of the auxiliary means. It is rather the lack of capacity for generalization, and, connected with this, what is formally far-fetched ('das formal Hergeholte'). The sentence 'Das wahrhaft Unbefriedigende besteht ...' breaks off and continues on the following page.

No mathematical content needs reconstructing.

results.what: Aphorism that purity of method matters less than generalizability: a foreign auxiliary method is not objectionable per se; what is unsatisfying is lack of generalizability and formal far-fetchedness.
results.modern_name: Purity of method / methodological purity in proof (philosophy of mathematical practice)
results.usually_credited_to: Discussed in the Hilbert tradition (cf. Grundlagen der Geometrie, 1899, on Reinheit der Methode). Modern discussions by Detlefsen, Arana, Mancosu and Hallett cite Hilbert's notebooks.

results.what: Mathematics stands on two legs: magnitude (function theory, geometry, physics) and the formal/divisibility side (number theory, reducibility); both are needed.
results.modern_name: Hilbert's dichotomy of Grössenbegriff vs. Zerlegungsbegriff (continuum/analysis vs. arithmetic/algebra)
results.usually_credited_to: Hilbert's notebooks (Cod. Ms. Hilbert 600), quoted in historical literature (e.g. Rowe, Corry)

results.what: Rebuttal of Goethe's 'Grau, teurer Freund, ist alle Theorie' (said by Mephistopheles) and the maxim 'the formula must be our servant'.
results.usually_credited_to: Hilbert (notebook aphorisms); the Faust quotation is Goethe's

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains purely philosophical aphorisms from Hilbert's well-known notebooks. Their themes (purity of method, the unity of arithmetic and analysis, the defence of theory) are characteristic of Hilbert and have been quoted in the historical and philosophical literature. There is no mathematical result here.

The Faust quotation is properly 'Grau, theurer Freund, ist alle Theorie' (Goethe, Faust I); the manuscript omits the commas.
The '&' before 'wie anders schreitet' appears in the image as an insertion or cross mark (✗), possibly a reference sign, rather than an ampersand.
'Thnecht'/'Thnechte' visually = 'Knecht'/'Knechte' (old-style K); the transcription is correct.
'Preinheit' visually = 'Reinheit' (Reinheit der Methode); the transcription is correct.
The opening bracket before 'Functionentheorie' is a square bracket closed by a round parenthesis in the manuscript, as transcribed.
